subject: Renewal: upgrade to 32 GPU reserved pool / pricing and SLA
messages:
From: Priya Desai <p.desai@synthhealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal discussion: capacity upgrade request

Hi Jasmine,

Hope you're well. We're coming up on our annual renewal for the Dedicated pool and our usage has consistently run above our 16-GPU commit during peak hours. After running a few load tests and discussing with engineering, we want to evaluate upgrading to a 32-GPU reserved pool effective the start of Q3.

Key asks from our side:
- Firm per-hour reserved pricing for 32 GPUs (we need number to feed procurement)
- Throughput/latency expectations at the pool level and any guarantees you can provide
- How a term change (we prefer a 12-month commitment) would affect price and credits for unused capacity
- Timeline for migration / CS involvement and whether there will be a short overlap period for burst crediting

I've attached our utilization report for Q1 to give you context (SynthHealth_Utilization_Report_Q1.pdf). Procurement is targeting a signed amendment by end of April, so any preliminary numbers this week would help.

Thanks,
Priya
Director of ML Platform
SynthHealth

Hi Priya — thanks for the context and the utilization report, that was very helpful. Happy to run these numbers with you and get procurement what they need.

High-level response and next steps:
1) Pricing snapshot (preliminary, for procurement planning):
   - 32-GPU reserved pool: $2.95 / GPU-hour (applies to committed hours in the reserved pool).
   - If you sign a 12-month amendment we can move to $2.75 / GPU-hour (volume discount).
   - We can also offer a 3-month transitional window at $2.85 / GPU-hour to start while you validate throughput.

2) Throughput & SLA:
   - For a dedicated 32-GPU pool we guarantee pool-level availability (SLA) and will commit to a throughput baseline: sustained median token throughput metrics are included in the SLA addendum. Concretely, our standard commitment for this size pool is a 95th-percentile request latency target and a sustained pool throughput floor sufficient for your reported peak utilization (we'll quantify in the addendum).

3) Migration & coordination:
   - Monica (CS) will own migration runbook and scheduling. We'll plan a two-week validation window with prefix/KV cache warmup and one week of overlap/burst credits to smooth cutover.

4) Next steps:
   - I'll prepare a formal quote and SLA addendum (PDF) and send a DocuSign link. Can you confirm: 12-month term is preferred, and target effective date 2026-07-01?

I'll attach a draft quote and SLA addendum in my next message.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the rapid reply, Jasmine — and hi Aditya. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the numbers:

- Our procurement team needs a single per-hour figure that we can put in the amendment. The $2.95 (or $2.75 for 12mo) structure is fine; procurement would prefer the 12-month firm price to be the definitive line item.
- The one-time credit sounds useful — would that reduce the first invoice or appear as a service credit? Procurement prefers invoice reduction if possible.
- For the SLA, we need explicit metrics in the addendum: pool-level p95 latency target for request completion and a declared minimum sustained tokens/sec throughput for the pool during peak (our SREs will validate).
- Migration: the two-week validation + one-week overlap is acceptable. We also need audit logs and access to token-level cost breakdowns for the migration period.

Procurement is still pushing for a signed amendment by 2026-04-28. Can you provide the formal quote and DocuSign by 2026-03-30?

Thanks,
Priya
